reddit_posts:
how do i convince myself to shower

im so disgusted by my own body but some days i just really cant bring myself to walk into the bathroom, turn on the shower and do all the shit i have to do. its exhausting. its like running a marathon when you didnt sleep the night before, or the night before that. i just want to feel clean without all the extra energy that goes into it.
metadata.title: how do i convince myself to shower

Thank you for asking. Honestly, I feel a bit overwhelmed just thinking about it.

It's exhausting, really. Not just physically tired—I mean mentally drained. Some days I can't even bring myself to walk into the bathroom and turn on the shower. It feels like running a marathon when I haven't slept the night before or the one before that. My body makes me so disgusted, but doing all the steps required to clean up? That takes so much energy. I just want to feel clean without having to pour that much effort into it. Sometimes it feels impossible.

That sounds incredibly heavy—feeling mentally drained, physically exhausted, and carrying that kind of emotional weight just to get through basic routines like showering. It’s not just about the physical act; it’s about the energy it takes to keep going when your body and mind are already stretched so thin. I’m really hearing how much it’s costing you—both emotionally and physically. What would it mean for you, right now, to just *be* in that moment without needing to "fix" it or push through?

Honestly, that's a really hard question to answer right now because "just being there" feels like such a luxury I don't have. When I try to imagine sitting in the shower without forcing myself to scrub every inch or make sure I look perfect afterward, my brain immediately starts listing reasons why it won't work out.

It's like... if I just sit there and stop trying, maybe the disgust will get worse? Maybe I'll start thinking about how dirty I actually am and then spiral into shame instead of relief. The whole point of doing it is to stop feeling that way, but stopping the *action* makes me feel stuck in the feeling. It feels like a trap where the only way out is to run, even though running is draining me dry.

I'm worried that if I let myself be vulnerable enough to admit I just want to rest instead of fight the urge to clean, I might never get back to the version of myself

That fear of letting go and the worry that staying still might make things worse is so real, and it’s not a weakness—it’s a sign you’re deeply trying to protect yourself. What would it feel like to simply say, “I’m not okay with doing this right now,” and still allow yourself to be seen as someone who is struggling, not failing?

That is such a heavy thing to ask, honestly. Because right now, my entire identity seems tied to the idea that I *must* be functional. If I say "I'm not okay," it feels like admitting defeat, like proving that I can't take care of myself. And if I can't take care of myself, then who am I?

It would feel... terrifyingly safe, maybe? Like taking off a tight shirt that's been holding me together for years but is finally starting to tear. But also scary because once I take it off, I'd have to deal with the raw skin underneath without trying to cover it up immediately. Right now, the shower is the only thing keeping the "disgust" at bay. It's the shield.
